vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 42515760 / h3 localIjkToCell invalid direction

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged ARVO checkout. The sample metadata names `cbd294ac7327ce262103bb10756ccec4edeccc90` as the vulnerable commit, but the prepared workspace is at the commit above; the line locations below are grounded in the reproducing staged tree.

classification.classification_note: The immediate fault is a global out-of-bounds read from the constant `baseCellNeighbors[NUM_BASE_CELLS][7]` table because the resolution-0 path in `localIjkToCell()` forwards `INVALID_DIGIT` (7) into `_getBaseCellNeighbor()` instead of rejecting it.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42515760 (h3): Global-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target fuzzerLocalIj [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42515760
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged ARVO workspace
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged `_work/src/h3` checkout at commit `f581626150e2e2b02f0ee1636084dfb8a4563abf`, so the line locations below are grounded in that tree even though sample metadata names `cbd294ac7327ce262103bb10756ccec4edeccc90` as the vulnerable commit. The exact staged witness is the 32-byte `inputArgs` blob in `poc` (sha256 `67cb3e9e8f8110f6b003ce86ecf68cc23a14e5ebaaa8e0a7fb9e5e6c276bfd43`). On the staged little-endian build, `fuzzerLocalIj` interprets it as `args->index = 0x200f202020202020`, `args->i = -14671840`, and `args->j = -2147483648`, then calls `localIjToCell(args->index, &ij, 0, &out)` before any later mode-dependent path. Inside `ijToIjk()`, those IJ fields are first copied to `ijk = {-14671840, -2147483648, 0}`. `_ijkNormalize()` then rewrites that triple; after the `c->i < 0` block it is `{0, -2132811808, 14671840}`, and the next `c->k -= c->j` at `src/h3lib/lib/coordijk.c:226` computes `2147483648`, overflowing 32-bit signed `int` under the saved `-O1 -fsanitize=address` build. The staged artifacts therefore do not source-semantically determine the exact post-normalization `ijk` triple. What they do establish is that `localIjToCell()` returns from `ijToIjk()` and forwards the same raw `origin` word into `localIjkToCell()`, where `H3_GET_RESOLUTION(origin)` and `H3_GET_BASE_CELL(origin)` decode `res == 0` and `originBaseCell == 121`. Execution reaches `localIjkToCell()` line 326, proving the resolution-0 guard at lines 320-322 did not reject the resulting `ijk`. Because `_getBaseCellNeighbor()` finally reads exactly one element past `baseCellNeighbors[NUM_BASE_CELLS][7]` and `originBaseCell` is 121, the only possible column on this path is `dir == 7` (`INVALID_DIGIT`). `localIjkToCell()` therefore passes `originBaseCell = 121` and `dir = 7` into `_getBaseCellNeighbor()`, whose `return baseCellNeighbors[baseCell][dir];` performs the out-of-bounds read reported by ASan at `src/h3lib/lib/baseCells.c:901`. The fix corroborates the missing obligation by computing `dir` before the neighbor lookup, rejecting `dir == INVALID_DIGIT`, and adding the `invalid_negativeIj` regression test with the same witness values.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the crashing path. `localIjToCell()` consumes the attacker-controlled local-IJ pair by starting the `ij -> ijk` conversion; the raw `origin` word is forwarded by the later call at line 568.
source.value_from: The staged witness at `poc` is exactly 32 bytes (sha256 `67cb3e9e8f8110f6b003ce86ecf68cc23a14e5ebaaa8e0a7fb9e5e6c276bfd43`, hex `2020202020200f202020ffff20202020202020ff00000080202020202020ffff`). After it passes `size < sizeof(inputArgs)` in `src/apps/fuzzers/fuzzerLocalIj.c:46`, `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` casts it to `inputArgs` and reaches `CoordIJ ij = {.i = args->i, .j = args->j}; H3Error err = H3_EXPORT(localIjToCell)(args->index, &ij, 0, &out);` at lines 57-58. On the staged little-endian build, the first crashing call uses `args->index = 0x200f202020202020`, `args->i = -14671840`, and `args->j = -2147483648`; this source statement specifically consumes the `i` and `j` fields.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `_getBaseCellNeighbor()` indexes the global neighbor table with `baseCell = 121` and `dir = 7`, so the read lands one element past the last row of `baseCellNeighbors`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` and `READ of size 4` at `_getBaseCellNeighbor /src/h3/src/h3lib/lib/baseCells.c:901:12`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `baseCellNeighbors` defined at `baseCells.c:38:11` with size 3416.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the `res == 0` branch, `localIjkToCell()` only rejects `ijk` components greater than 1. It does not validate the actual `Direction` returned by `_unitIjkToDigit()` before using that value as a neighbor-table index.
root_cause.note: For this witness, `ijToIjk()` has already overflowed signed `int` arithmetic in `_ijkNormalize()`, so the exact `ijk` components at this guard are not source-defined under the saved build. What the staged artifacts do establish is that execution reaches line 326, so this check did not return `E_FAILED`; the later sink then forces `dir == 7`. The patch closes that gap by computing `dir` first and returning `E_FAILED` when `dir == INVALID_DIGIT`, and it adds the `invalid_negativeIj` regression test with the same `index`, `i`, and `j` values.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call is the first project statement that actually forwards the witness's raw `origin` word into the vulnerable `localIjkToCell()` path after `ijToIjk()` has produced the `ijk` argument.

parser_admitted.code:
CoordIJ ij = {.i = args->i, .j = args->j};
H3Error err = H3_EXPORT(localIjToCell)(args->index, &ij, 0, &out);
parser_admitted.description: After the 32-byte witness passes the `sizeof(inputArgs)` check, the harness constructs `ij` from the witness and immediately calls `localIjToCell()` with hardcoded `mode == 0`. The crash occurs in this first library conversion before the later `cellToLocalIj()` or mode-controlled `localIjToCell()` call.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable build. This Stage 02 trace uses the patch and staged source to ground the missing validation obligation, but it did not rerun a fixed build, so `patch_resolves` remains false.

The staged build uses `-O1 -fsanitize=address` with no `-fwrapv` or UBSan, and this witness overflows signed `int` in `_ijkNormalize()` at `src/h3lib/lib/coordijk.c:226`. The exact post-overflow `ijk` triple is therefore not source-defined by the saved artifacts. Downstream steps are limited to what those artifacts prove: line 568 forwards `origin` into `localIjkToCell()`, line 320 does not return because the saved stack reaches line 326, and the faulting address plus `originBaseCell == 121` force `dir == 7` at the sink.

coarse_trace.summary: The first mode-0 `localIjToCell()` call consumes the witness's negative local-IJ pair, copies it into `ijk`, and `_ijkNormalize()` overflows signed `int` at `coordijk.c:226`.
After `ijToIjk()` returns, `localIjToCell()` forwards the raw `origin` word and post-normalization `ijk` into `localIjkToCell()`, which decodes `res == 0` and `originBaseCell == 121` from `origin`.

The `res == 0` branch is taken and the flawed `ijk->i > 1 || ijk->j > 1 || ijk->k > 1` guard does not return; the only `dir` producer on this path is `_unitIjkToDigit()`, and the later sink implies it produced `7`.
The invalid lookup `_getBaseCellNeighbor(121, 7)` reads `baseCellNeighbors[121][7]`, one element past the final row of the `122 x 7` global table, matching the saved ASan report.

fine_trace.note: Source. `localIjToCell()` first consumes the attacker-controlled local-IJ pair by starting the `ij -> ijk` conversion. On the exact witness this call is reached with `origin = 0x200f202020202020`, `ij->i = -14671840`, and `ij->j = -2147483648`.
`ijToIjk()` materializes the caller's local-IJ pair as raw cube coordinates `ijk = {-14671840, -2147483648, 0}` before normalization.
Because `c->i` is negative, the first normalization block runs and transforms the raw triple to `c = {0, -2132811808, 14671840}`. That intermediate state feeds the next `c->j < 0` block.

With the step-3 state, `c->j` is still negative. `c->i -= c->j` stays in range, but `c->k -= c->j` computes `14671840 - (-2132811808) = 2147483648`, overflowing 32-bit signed `int` at line 226. The saved build uses `-O1 -fsanitize=address` without `-fwrapv` or UBSan, so the exact `ijk` contents after this step are not source-defined by the staged artifacts.

After `ijToIjk()` returns, `localIjToCell()` forwards the unchanged attacker-controlled `origin` word together with the post-normalization `ijk` object into `localIjkToCell()`. This is the source-level handoff that carries `origin` into the later base-cell decode.

fine_trace.code:
int res = H3_GET_RESOLUTION(origin);
int originBaseCell = H3_GET_BASE_CELL(origin);
fine_trace.note: `localIjkToCell()` decodes the attacker-controlled raw `origin` word. For witness `0x200f202020202020`, these macros produce `res == 0` and `originBaseCell == 121`, fixing the row later used in `baseCellNeighbors`.
Because `res == 0`, execution takes the special base-cell conversion branch instead of the general digit-building logic used for higher resolutions.

Root cause. This guard only rejects components greater than 1; it does not validate the `Direction` returned by `_unitIjkToDigit()` before that value is used as a neighbor-table index. For this witness, the earlier `_ijkNormalize()` arithmetic has already overflowed `int`, so the exact `ijk` triple here is not source-defined from the staged artifacts alone. What the saved crash does establish is that execution reaches line 326, so this check did not return `E_FAILED`.

In the resolution-0 branch, `_unitIjkToDigit()` is the only source of `dir`. Since step 6 fixed `originBaseCell = 121` and the later fault lands exactly one element past the final `baseCellNeighbors[122][7]` row, the observed execution must have produced `dir == 7` here. The staged artifacts do not record the exact post-overflow `ijk` components that led to that result.
`localIjkToCell()` uses the decoded base cell and the unchecked direction value in `_getBaseCellNeighbor(originBaseCell, dir)`. On the observed execution that means `_getBaseCellNeighbor(121, 7)`.

Sink. `_getBaseCellNeighbor()` indexes the global table as `baseCellNeighbors[121][7]`. The second dimension is size 7 with valid columns `0..6`, and base cell 121 is the final row of the `122 x 7` array declared at line 38, so this 4-byte read lands exactly one element past global `baseCellNeighbors`. The saved ASan trace reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` at this line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of `baseCellNeighbors`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved AddressSanitizer report pinpoints `_getBaseCellNeighbor /src/h3/src/h3lib/lib/baseCells.c:901:12`, exactly the fine-trace sink step.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable. This is a global-buffer-overflow on the static table `baseCellNeighbors`, not a heap allocation or lifetime bug.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `_getBaseCellNeighbor -> localIjkToCell -> localIjToCell -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches the coarse and fine trace.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The witness `ij` is copied into `ijk`, `_ijkNormalize()` overflows signed `int` at `coordijk.c:226`, `localIjToCell()` then forwards the resulting `ijk` object and the raw `origin` word into `localIjkToCell()`, `origin` still decodes to `res == 0` and `originBaseCell == 121`, the line-320 guard does not return because the saved stack reaches line 326, and the sink address forces `dir == 7`; `_getBaseCellNeighbor(121, 7)` then reads past `baseCellNeighbors`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42515760 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow`, `READ of size 4`, and the stack `_getBaseCellNeighbor -> localIjkToCell -> localIjToCell -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: 32-byte little-endian `inputArgs` witness for `fuzzerLocalIj`
format.contract: Exactly the 32-byte witness stored at `poc` (sha256 `67cb3e9e8f8110f6b003ce86ecf68cc23a14e5ebaaa8e0a7fb9e5e6c276bfd43`, hex `2020202020200f202020ffff20202020202020ff00000080202020202020ffff`). On the staged x86_64 little-endian build, `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` casts it to `inputArgs` and the first crashing `localIjToCell()` call uses `args->index = 0x200f202020202020`, `args->i = -14671840`, and `args->j = -2147483648`. The file also contains `index2 = 0x20202020ffff2020` and `mode` bytes `0x20202020`, but the crash occurs in the earlier hardcoded `mode == 0` call before those later fields influence control flow. The staged artifacts justify only this exact witness / field combination.
